text: A gap in the wall, where the stones have gone for a walk. {lead} fits them back one by one, like a very slow jigsaw. Tucked in the wall behind: Four-Leaf Clover.
The wheel has been here since last spring's chase. {lead} sets it rolling, and underneath is Tin Penny-Farthing.
{lead} peers into the water, then pulls out, with great ceremony, Sea Glass.
A peat pool, black as tea. {lead} dives in, flippers going, and comes up spluttering and delighted with a purse, a bit damp.
{lead} skims a stone over the pool and a bottle on a post tips over. Hanging from it: Ammonite.
A coracle, tied up and patient. {lead} takes the paddle and you take a seat. The water is easy and the other side has Ammonite.
The bog water is dark and cold. {lead} ploughs through it with its face down and surfaces holding a purse, a bit damp.
A glint under the surface, just out of reach. {lead} hooks it with patience and a bit of reed. It is Roach.
A dead trunk, leaning on nothing much. {lead} puts its shoulder to it and over it goes with a crack. Underneath: Oak Acorn.
The bog water is dark and cold. {lead} ploughs through it with its face down and surfaces holding a roll of notes.
The little round boat wobbles, then settles. {lead} crosses the water with short, careful strokes and lands among the reeds. There is Sea Glass.
A wall with a tooth missing. {lead} rebuilds it with no mortar and a great deal of dignity, and finds Slate Chips in the hollow.
